resources.string: Records from the aids. The next press on either aid ends it. Set where it goes on the Voice screen.

Map Voice note to a press on the Buttons screen. That press starts recording from the aids\' microphones. The next press on either aid stops it, and which press you use decides where the note goes. Every note is saved first, whatever happens after.
Voice notes need the microphone permission.
Open the app once to record in the background
Android only lets the app use the microphone in the background after it has been on screen since the phone started. Keep this screen open for a moment and it is ready.
No press starts a voice note yet
On the Buttons screen, set a press, for example a long press on the left aid, to Voice note.
The press mapped to Voice note starts a recording.
While a note records, any press on either aid ends it. Pick where each press sends the note. It is always saved too.
When this press ends a note
Webhook and White Noise appear here once they are set up under Advanced.
Keep the recording on the phone.
Save, then send to your chosen White Noise group.
Save, then post to your webhook URL.
Save, then open the share sheet. With the phone locked it waits behind a notification.
A minute before the limit you hear a warning. At the limit the note ends as a short press on the aid that started it would.
Sends the recording only. Nothing is transcribed.
Transcribes on the phone and sends both. The transcript is saved next to the recording.
Sends only the transcript. The recording and transcript are still saved. If transcription fails, the audio is sent instead.
Install Offline Speech to Text (Zapstore) and download a model in it. Transcription runs on the phone, offline.

While their microphones are open the aids switch to a call-like mode. Music sounds flatter until the note ends. The aids offer a microphone only while they are the phone\'s active audio device. If other Bluetooth headphones are active, their microphone is used, and with none, the phone\'s.
Recordings (.m4a) and transcripts (.txt) are saved here, so a sync app like Syncthing can pick them up.
A note whose sending failed keeps its saved copy. Retry sends it again.
Webhook and White Noise need network access. Turn on Network for I Hear You in its app settings.
Network access is off for I Hear You (app settings, Network).
Posts each note as multipart form data: metadata (JSON), transcript (text) and audio (.m4a). Works with n8n, Home Assistant or your own server. Any 2xx reply counts as delivered.
I Hear You gets its own White Noise identity. Invite it into a group, for example one with your AI agent, and notes ended with the White Noise press are sent there.
In White Noise, add this npub to a group. The invite appears below. Agents such as Hermes must also allow this npub to invite and message them.
No groups yet. Accept an invite first.
Replies stay in the group; nothing is played.
Messages in the group are played into the aids for %1$d minutes after you send a note: voice replies as they are, text read aloud. A short press stops a reply.
Every new message in the group is played into the aids. A short press stops a reply.
Open I Hear You once so it can use the microphone in the background.
Check the microphone toggle, whether the aids are muted, or whether a call or another app has the microphone. Recording continues.
What was recorded until then is saved.
The recording is saved (%1$s). Retry sends it again.

The nsec is the private key of this app\'s identity: whoever has it can write as this app. Keep it in a password manager. Importing it restores the identity (the same npub), not the groups: after an import, the groups have to invite the npub again.
This replaces the current identity. Its groups are dropped and the voice-note group is cleared; the groups have to invite the imported npub again.
Identity imported. Invite its npub to the groups again.
Voice replies play as they are, text replies are read by the phone\'s voice.
Only voice replies play; text replies stay in the group. Ask the agent to answer in voice.
Comma-separated. A reply containing any of these is not played, for example the 🎙️ that marks the transcript of your own voice note.
Voice notes work much better with Offline Speech to Text: a free app that turns speech into text on the phone, offline.
The URL must start with https://. Android does not let I Hear You send to http://, and the note would travel unencrypted.
I Hear You is no longer in this group. Pick another one, or have it invited again.
Group members see this name next to your notes. Make it say whose it is, for example \"I Hear You (Anna)\".
Name published. Other apps may take a while to show it.
No speech recognised. The recognizer on this phone cannot transcribe a recording: install Offline Speech to Text (free, on Zapstore).
